To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Kozak sequence has an important influence on the expression of foreign genes in horse cells in culture.

the expression of a gene in horse cells in culture can be increased by inserting the gene between a CMV promoter and a CMV intron, and further increased by inserting a Kozak consensus sequence immediately upstream of the gene.
a Kozak consensus sequence upstream of the start codon of an expression cassette is essential for the expression of proteins in horse cells in tissue culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of vectors for efficient gene expression in horse cells for DNA vaccination.
the development of DNA vaccine vectors that are efficiently and stably expressed in primary horse cells.
the development of efficient vectors for gene transfer and DNA vaccination in horses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Kozak sequences in the vectors are important for efficient gene expression in horse cells.
the pUC vector containing the CMV promoter and intron A and the Kozak sequence is the most efficient for ectopic expression in horse cells.

the Kozak sequence is essential for protein expression in horses in vitro and that the pUC vector with the CMV intron and a Kozak upstream of the gene is the most suitable vector for in vitro DNA vaccination in horses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pcDNA3.1 vectors without CMV intron and with a Kozak consensus sequence upstream of the coding sequence are the most suitable for expression of foreign genes in horse cells in culture.
the pcDNA vectors are more efficient than the pUC vectors in terms of expression in horse cells.
the pUC vectors with a Kozak consensus sequence upstream of the human serum protein gene are the most efficient in vitro expression vectors for primary horse cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
horse cells are very sensitive to the Kozak sequences in the expression vectors.
the use of the pUC CMV vectors in horses may be problematic and the pcDNA CMV vectors may not necessarily be the best choice either.
the use of the CMV intron is not a prerequisite for high level expression of genes in horse cells in culture.
